requirement:
Colon directive fences use three or more colons and support nested directives
with shorter inner fences. A colon-only closing fence has at least as many
colons as its opener, followed only by optional whitespace.
Backtick and tilde code fences follow CommonMark rules and shield their contents
from colon-directive recognition. Fence-like text in inline code or raw HTML
introduces no outline directive blocks.
rationale:
structural: `requirements.sdk.sources.markdown.fence_precedence` states only observable parsing behavior, so I found no structural obligation that needs implementation evidence. It has no implementation edges and no review roots.

I checked each clause against an alternative implementation that gives the same results:
- "Colon directive fences use three or more colons and support nested directives with shorter inner fences." This describes which inputs are recognized. A hand-written scanner, a parser library or a regex would all meet it.
- "A colon-only closing fence has at least as many colons as its opener, followed only by optional whitespace." This is a matching rule on input. The code structure is free.
- "Backtick and tilde code fences follow CommonMark rules and shield their contents from colon-directive recognition." This names CommonMark as a behavioral standard. It does not name a required library, type or interface. Any implementation with the same CommonMark fence behavior satisfies it.
- "Fence-like text in inline code or raw HTML introduces no outline directive blocks." This describes output behavior only.

The clauses name no required library, algorithm, signature, type, field or delegation interface. Tests supply evidence for the behavioral obligations.

behavioral: All obligations of `requirements.sdk.sources.markdown.fence_precedence` are covered by the five tests in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/markdown_tests.rs`. The tests are marked with `{test}` references, and each one asserts concrete outcomes.

- **Three or more colons and nesting with shorter inner fences.**
  - `unfinished_directives_retain_their_body_and_leave_the_outer_closer_outside` nests a three-colon tip inside a six-colon note. It asserts two blocks, their line ranges, the parent relationship, and that the inner block does not contain the outer closer.
  - `nested_fence_lengths_and_closer_whitespace_preserve_the_right_containers` nests a four-colon tip inside a six-colon note and asserts the block count, line ranges and parents.
  - `two_colons_and_inline_directive_text_do_not_open_containers` shows that a two-colon fence, a directive with a blank name, inline text before a fence, and a bare three-colon line open no block.
- **A closer needs at least as many colons as its opener.**
  - In `nested_fence_lengths_and_closer_whitespace_preserve_the_right_containers`, a three-colon line does not close the four-colon tip. The tip block ends only at the later four-colon closer.
  - In `empty_long_closed_and_quoted_directives_keep_original_unicode_offsets`, a five-colon line closes a three-colon opener.
  - The unfinished-directive test shows a six-colon closer closes the outer opener, which is the longer-closer case.
- **A closer is followed only by optional whitespace.** The nested-fence test asserts that a four-colon line followed by trailing text does not close the tip, because the tip extends to the later four-colon line with trailing spaces.
- **Backtick and tilde code fences follow CommonMark and shield colon directives.**
  - `literal_code_inline_code_and_html_shield_directive_looking_text` covers four-backtick and four-tilde fences. A shorter fence line and a colon closer inside them do not end the fence, and the tests assert no paragraph or extra block appears.
  - The same test covers a backtick directive fence containing an inner colon directive.
  - The nested-fence test puts a tilde fence containing colon fences and a fake directive inside a container, then asserts the fake directive is not a block and the owner at the relevant line is the enclosing block.
- **Inline code and raw HTML introduce no directive blocks.** The shield test covers a multi-line code span, a `<div>` HTML block, an HTML comment, and single-line inline code. It asserts that no block node exists in any of them.

I found no obligation without a test, and no assertion that contradicts the requirement. I did not treat edge cases the text doesn't name as gaps. Examples are tab whitespace on a closer and indented fences.
